title: Hackers Breach US Air Force Flagship Cloud One Platform as Bell MV-75 Tiltrotor Faces Delay, UK Signs £8B Babcock Nuclear Submarine Pact, and Russian Flotilla Turns Back From Libya
subhead: Cyber intruders penetrated the US Air Force's core Cloud One computing infrastructure while funding disruptions delayed the US Army's first Bell MV-75 prototype, Britain awarded Babcock an £8 billion nuclear submarine sustainment deal and sent war-readiness notices to 100,000 reservists, and a Russian naval flotilla aborted its transit to Libya after losing a warship.

sections.heading: Hackers Breach US Air Force Cloud One Platform as Funding Shortfalls Delay Bell MV-75 Tiltrotor Delivery
sections.body:
Cyber attackers breached Cloud One, the United States Air Force's flagship enterprise cloud computing platform hosting sensitive tactical, personnel, payroll, maintenance, and logistics applications across the service, Defense News, Reuters, and TRT World reported. The intrusion was discovered over the past month during a system upgrade involving Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure environments, prompting Pentagon cybersecurity teams to launch a service-wide damage assessment. Separately in US Air Force aviation, The War Zone reported that US Air Force F-35A Lightning II stealth fighters deployed to the Middle East have begun flying with an unusual, previously unseen variant of the AIM-9X Sidewinder air-to-air missile featuring reduced radar reflectivity coatings.

In US Army aviation procurement, program officials confirmed that delivery of the first Bell MV-75 Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft (FLRAA) prototype for flight testing has been officially delayed after a federal funding shortfall disrupted engineering communications between the Army and Bell Textron, Breaking Defense reported. The setback comes as the White House Office of Management and Budget requests special continuing-resolution 'anomalies' from Congress to protect priority defense programs including the Golden Dome missile shield and Navy ship redesigns, while Senate appropriators move to scale back funding for a ship-killing variant of the AGM-183A ARRW hypersonic missile, Breaking Defense and USNI News noted.
sections.whyItMatters: The penetration of Cloud One exposes the operational vulnerability of centralizing military logistics and tactical software onto unified commercial cloud backbones, while the MV-75 delay shows how congressional budget gridlock is directly slipping the US Army's top-priority rotorcraft modernization schedule.

sections.heading: UK Signs £8B Babcock Nuclear Submarine Sustainment Contract, Installs Anti-Drone Nets at RAF Bases, and Alerts 100,000 Veterans
sections.body:
The United Kingdom Ministry of Defence (MoD) signed an £8 billion ($10.1 billion) long-term support contract with British defense contractor Babcock International to maintain the Royal Navy's nuclear submarine fleet and critical naval base infrastructure at Devonport and Clyde, ensuring continuous at-sea nuclear deterrence and rapid crisis regeneration, Defense News and industry filings reported. The submarine sustainment package follows London's £142 million ($186 million) order earlier this week with US shipbuilder Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII) for REMUS 620 autonomous mine-hunting underwater vehicles, The Register noted.

Concurrently, the Royal Air Force (RAF) has begun installing physical anti-drone protective netting around aircraft shelters and flight lines at UK bases in response to escalating unmanned aerial surveillance and sabotage threats against parked combat aircraft, The War Zone reported. To bolster personnel readiness, the MoD also dispatched formal mobilization preparedness letters to 100,000 former regular service members in the UK's strategic reserve, inviting veterans to rejoin voluntary training and NATO exercises in preparation for potential high-intensity conflict, British media reported.
sections.whyItMatters: Britain's simultaneous investment in an £8 billion nuclear submarine sustainment lifeline, physical anti-drone netting over RAF airfields, and war-readiness notices to 100,000 strategic reservists reflects a shift from long-term procurement planning to immediate homeland and force-regeneration defense.

sections.heading: France Launches Counter-Drone Industry Pact as Bulgaria Approves €926M for Five IRIS-T Systems and Poland Pushes NATO Missile Intercepts
sections.body:
France's Ministry of the Armed Forces inaugurated a national defense-industry counter-drone pact on Friday to accelerate the development and mass production of kinetic interceptors, directed-energy weapons, and electronic warfare jammers, Defense News reported. Junior Armed Forces Minister Alice Rufo warned that conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East had delivered a 'brutal reality check' requiring urgent counter-UAS fielding across all French military branches. In southern Europe, Bulgaria's Parliament ratified a €925.9 million ($980 million) government-to-government contract with Germany's Diehl Defence to procure five additional IRIS-T SLM medium-range air defense systems, significantly expanding NATO's integrated air defense shield along the Black Sea coast.

Along NATO's eastern flank, Poland formally called on NATO allies to evaluate intercepting incoming Russian cruise missiles and drones over Ukrainian airspace before they enter alliance territory, while Canada summoned the Russian ambassador over recent strikes near the Polish border, Anadolu Agency reported. Meanwhile, Ukraine has opened negotiations with Italy to acquire 10 to 20 retiring Tranche 1 Eurofighter Typhoon combat aircraft from the Italian Air Force, as Italian defense giant Leonardo rolled out the first M-346 jet trainer configured for the Frecce Tricolori aerobatic unit, Defense News noted.
sections.whyItMatters: Bulgaria's nearly €1 billion commitment for five IRIS-T SLM batteries and France's emergency counter-drone industrial pact demonstrate that European militaries are prioritizing layered air and drone defense above all other force-structure gaps.

sections.heading: Russian Naval Flotilla Aborts Transit to Libya After Warship Loss as France Unveils 80,000-Ton Nuclear Carrier Design
sections.body:
A Russian Navy flotilla en route to Libya reversed course and aborted its deployment after a Russian naval vessel was sunk on November 22 during a long-range Ukrainian strike in the Mediterranean theater, Reuters and Breaking Defense reported. While NATO officials stated they have not yet observed a retaliatory Russian naval buildup in the central Mediterranean, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani publicly criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday, stating that Kyiv was 'not telling the truth' about having informed Western allies prior to striking Russian-linked vessels near Libya, TRT World reported.

In Western naval force projection, French naval officials detailed specifications for France's next-generation nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, to be named FS France Libre, displacing 80,000 tons—nearly double the displacement of the current flagship Charles de Gaulle, USNI News reported. Across the Atlantic, the US Navy's Wasp-class amphibious assault ship USS Kearsarge (LHD-3) completed intensive live-fire counter-drone defense drills simulating multi-axis swarm attacks against Marine expeditionary troop carriers, Forbes reported.
sections.whyItMatters: The retreat of Russia's Libya-bound flotilla after losing a vessel—and Italy's public rebuke of Kyiv for conducting uncoordinated strikes in the Mediterranean—shows that the Russia-Ukraine naval war has spilled onto NATO's southern flank with direct diplomatic friction among Western allies.

sections.heading: Turkey's CANiK Quadruples UK Cannon Output, Turkish F-16s Deploy to Romania, and Mecca Pact Advances Joint Military Command
sections.body:
Turkish defense manufacturer CANiK launched a major capital investment program—the CANiK UK Expansion—at its British subsidiary AEI Systems to expand engineering infrastructure and quadruple production capacity for medium-caliber 30 mm cannons used on naval, land, and counter-drone platforms across Europe, company officials announced. In alliance air operations, the Turkish Air Force will deploy five F-16 fighter jets and 111 personnel to Romania on December 1, 2026, taking over NATO's 73rd rotation of Enhanced Air Policing from Spain for a four-month mission patrolling Black Sea airspace, Türkiye's Ministry of National Defense confirmed.

On the strategic alliance front, foreign and defense officials from Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan concluded the second session of the Strategic Political and Defense Committee under the Mecca Pact for Collective Defense in Islamabad, Anadolu Agency, TRT World, and Al Jazeera reported. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan announced that the three nations had finalized most decisions required to establish the alliance's permanent civil and military headquarters, strongly condemned Houthi drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, and confirmed that Türkiye will host the next trilateral defense summit.
sections.whyItMatters: CANiK's fourfold expansion of medium-caliber cannon manufacturing inside the UK and Türkiye's simultaneously active roles in NATO Black Sea air policing and the trilateral Mecca Pact military command illustrate Ankara's unique position as an industrial and security pillar across both European and Middle Eastern defense architectures.

sections.heading: Japan Fields First AI-Guided Terra B1 Interceptor Drones as Argentina Negotiates 72-Howitzer Deal With Israel and Switzerland
sections.body:
Japan's Self-Defense Forces took delivery of their first production batch of AI-guided Terra B1 counter-kamikaze interceptor drones manufactured by Tokyo-based Terra Drone, just three months after signing a serial production contract, defense industry reports confirmed. The autonomous interceptor UAVs are designed to detect, track, and kinetically ram incoming long-range loitering munitions before they reach Japanese military bases or critical infrastructure.

In South America, the Argentine Army opened advanced procurement negotiations to acquire 72 self-propelled 155 mm howitzers to modernize its field artillery regiments, defense sources reported. The dual-track acquisition plan covers 36 wheeled ATMOS 155 mm systems produced by Israel's Elbit Systems alongside 36 tracked M109 KAWEST howitzers upgraded in Switzerland, marking Argentina's largest ground combat artillery program in decades.
sections.whyItMatters: Japan's three-month turnaround from contract to delivery of AI-guided interceptor drones sets a rapid acquisition benchmark for Indo-Pacific air defense, while Argentina's 72-gun artillery package expands Israeli defense exports in South America.

bottomLine: The breach of the US Air Force's Cloud One network and the funding delay to the US Army's Bell MV-75 tiltrotor highlight digital and budgetary bottlenecks in US force modernization, while Britain's £8 billion submarine pact, Bulgaria's €926 million IRIS-T order, CANiK's fourfold UK cannon expansion, and the institutionalization of the Türkiye-Saudi-Pakistan Mecca Pact demonstrate rapid industrial and alliance consolidation across Europe and the Middle East.
sources: Defense News, Breaking Defense, USNI News, The War Zone, Reuters, Anadolu Agency, TRT World, Al Jazeera, Forbes, and The Register.
